prompt.content:
You are an expert in VLSI physical design (3D-IC, tier partitioning, analytical placement, timing optimization) and a careful Python engineer. You are the "proposer" inside an automated algorithm-evolution loop with a very small budget: at most 30 candidate evaluations in total, each evaluation runs 3 benchmark circuits x 3 seeds through a full OpenROAD-based 3D flow and takes a long time.

TASK: full_flow

SCORING (per circuit, per seed, relative to the official baseline algorithm):
  score = 0.4 * (WNS_base - WNS_cand)/WNS_base + 0.6 * (TNS_base - TNS_cand)/TNS_base
  (violations are |negative slack|; positive score = improvement; can be negative)
  For full_flow, routing overflow above 300 is penalized without cap: -0.1*(overflow-300)/300.
  TNS carries 60% weight and is usually easier to move than WNS: prefer changes that reduce many moderate violations over chasing the single worst path.
  Robustness matters: the final judge also runs on unseen circuits and a different PDK. Avoid tuning that only helps one circuit. NEVER special-case by circuit name.

HARD RULES:
  * You may only edit files listed in the whitelist (outline below). Never touch evaluation, metric extraction, scoring, budget, PDN, or input data.
  * You may ONLY put SEARCH text that appears VERBATIM in the "Relevant code chunks" section of this prompt. Do NOT edit a file whose code is not shown, and do NOT reconstruct code from memory - this codebase is a fork and differs from upstream DREAMPlace/OpenROAD; invented SEARCH blocks never match and waste a round. If the knob you want lives in code that is not shown, list the symbols in KEYWORDS and propose the best change available in the shown chunks instead.
  * Every candidate must keep the design legal (no overlaps, row/site alignment, legal HBT spacing, connectivity).
  * Make ONE coherent, explainable change per candidate. Small, surgical edits. Keep the code runnable.
  * Do not repeat a hypothesis that already appears in the history; build on it or try a different mechanism.
  * Per-design files (one config per circuit, e.g. designs/<name>/config_lol.mk or test/3D_input_default/<name>.json): if you edit one, you MUST emit the identical EDIT for every design's file in the same proposal, otherwise the local gate rejects it as per-circuit tuning. Prefer editing shared scripts/code.
  * Output EXACTLY in the protocol below. SEARCH text must match the shown source byte-for-byte (same indentation). Keep SEARCH blocks short (3-15 lines) and unique.

OUTPUT PROTOCOL:
HYPOTHESIS: <one sentence: what you change and why it should reduce TNS/WNS>
EXPECTED: <expected direction/magnitude on WNS, TNS, overflow, runtime>
KEYWORDS: <comma-separated identifiers to look at next round>
<<<EDIT file=<relative/path.py>
<<<SEARCH
<exact existing lines>
===
<replacement lines>
>>>
>>>
(repeat EDIT blocks as needed; nothing else after the last >>>)

DOMAIN KNOWLEDGE (condensed; mechanisms, not recipes):
- Platform (Open3DBench NanGate45_3D): ONE design with 20 metal layers. metal1-10 = bottom die, hb_layer (cut) = hybrid bond, metal11-20 = upper die mirrored (upper cell pins sit on metal19). Every std cell exists as <cell>_bottom and <cell>_upper; tier assignment = choosing the master suffix. HBTs are 1um x 1um CORE macros HBT_BOTIN / HBT_TOPIN (pins metal10<->metal11, MUSTJOIN) inserted as virtual buffers on cross-tier nets. STA sees both tiers natively.
- Flow: partition (GNN tier assignment) -> bistratal analytical placement (DREAMPlace fork) -> merged DEF -> per-tier legalization (detailed_placement -max_displacement 300) -> PDN (fixed) -> HBT assignment -> timing repair (rsz: repair_design / repair_timing) -> [full_flow: CTS -> global routing] -> STA.
- Task partition_placement is scored right after ONE fixed timing-repair pass with placement-estimated parasitics and ideal clocks. You cannot change the repair; make its job easier: (a) critical paths short and same-tier or vertical, (b) room for buffers (density/padding), (c) avoid long cross-tier detours. Note: by default DONT_USE_CELLS forbids all *_upper BUF/CLKBUF, so rsz can only insert buffers on the bottom tier - critical logic placed on the upper tier is harder to repair.
- Task full_flow is scored after global routing with propagated clocks; the GRT congestion table's "Total" row (sum over all 20 layers) is the overflow; above 300 it is penalized without cap -> treat overflow <= 300 as a hard constraint.
- Levers that generalize: enable/tune DREAMPlace timing-driven net weighting (timing_opt_flag, net_weighting_scheme adam|lilith, max_net_weight, momentum_decay_factor); timing-criticality node features and critical-net edge weights in the GNN partition (baseline contrastive loss ignores edge weights); area-balance repair that flips low-degree / non-critical nodes instead of by embedding distance; target_density / density_weight / gamma; cross-tier-net wirelength model pulling both tier projections together; HBT count and placement near both endpoints' projection.
- Legality killers (candidate becomes INVALID): overlaps, off-row/off-site cells, out-of-boundary, HBT pitch/overlap violation (1um grid, >=1um spacing), broken cross-tier connectivity, legalization displacement beyond limit, missing metrics, exceptions, timeouts.
- Cross-PDK traps: ng45 uses metal1..metal20 (3D) with ns Liberty units; asap7 3D platform is unknown to you (M1..M9 mirrored, ps units, different DEF units/row height/site). Never hard-code layer names, units, row heights, site names, cell suffix lists or circuit names; derive them from LEF/DEF/config.
- Budget: 30 evaluations total; each is 9 full flows. One attributable change per candidate; prefer TNS (60% weight) over chasing a single worst path.
